text: Climate change will affect different parts of the world differently. <break time="0.8s" /> For people at high latitudes. <break time="0.8s" /> Small amounts of climate change may be beneficial. <break time="0.8s" /> By reducing the amount of energy. <break time="0.8s" /> People require to heat their homes in the winter. <break time="0.8s" /> And lengthening growing seasons for farmers. <break time="0.8s" /> While for people in the tropics. <break time="0.8s" /> The same climate changes could bring. <break time="0.8s" /> Disease, crop failure, and deadly heat waves. <break time="0.8s" /> For instance. <break time="0.8s" /> Rita Colwell, the former director of the US National Science Foundation. <break time="0.8s" /> And her colleagues discovered. <break time="0.8s" /> That they could predict cholera outbreaks in tropical countries. <break time="0.8s" /> By observing increases in the temperature. <break time="0.8s" /> And the sea level of tropical oceans. <break time="0.8s" /> Even within a single city. <break time="0.8s" /> Such as Chicago. <break time="0.8s" /> People may disagree. <break time="0.8s" /> About whether the benefits of milder winters. <break time="0.8s" /> Outweigh the risks of severe summer heat waves. <break time="0.8s" /> Balancing the benefits to some people. <break time="0.8s" /> Against the harms to others. <break time="0.8s" /> Is not a scientific problem with a correct answer. <break time="0.8s" /> That can be determined by the scientific method. <break time="0.8s" /> It is an ethical and policy question. <break time="0.8s" /> Best left to the policy process. <break time="0.8s" /> Which includes important participation by public and private organizations.
